2. The petitioner is a citizen of Bangladesh and carrying on business as importer and distributor of food grains and crops including table potatoes through his proprietorship concern named and styled "M/s Panama Extension". The respondent No.1 is the Director, Plant Conservation Wing, Department of Agricultural Extension, the respondent No.2 is the Director General, Department of Agricultural Extension, the respondent No. 3 is the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture and the respondent No. 4 is Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Commerce. In the course of his business, the petitioner imported 300 metric tons of table potatoes from India. Accordingly, he applied to the respondent No. 1 for issuance of import permit under Rules 3 and 5 of the Destructive Insects and Pests Rules, 1966 framed pursuant to the powers delegated to the Government under section 3 of the Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914. The petitioner filed. an application on payment of requisite fees of Taka 310 through Government Treasury Chalan No. GaDa2/12 dated 29-10-2000. The said application form and chalan were forwarded under cover of a letter dated 29-10-2000. Having received no response whatsoever to the said application for import permits, the petitioner addressed a letter dated 1-11-2000 to the respondent . No. 1 requesting for issuance of the import permit on an urgent basis. Thereafter, the petitioner sent a reminder on 2-11-2000 requesting issuance of the import permit on an urgent basis. On 5-11-2000 the petitioner sent another letter to the respondent No.1 expressing his anxiety that the season for importation of table potatoes was passing and that unless import perm it facilitating importation of table potatoes was issued, the petitioner would be put to severe business losses. He also sought for hearing within 10-11-2000 to resolve the matter. Thereafter, petitioner addressed a letter dated 9-11-2000 to the respondent No. 4 in this connection seeking his intervention in the matter. It is stated that under Import Policy Order 1997-2002, an SRO issued by the respondent No. 4 under the Import Control Act, 1950, table potatoes are freely importable but seed potatoes are importable subject to the conditions as set out in Table 'Kha' of the Import Policy Order. The petitioner has learnt that the respondent No.4 in its meeting dated 28-8-2000 adopted a resolution to amend the Import Policy Order in order to subject the importation of table potatoes to the same conditions to which seed potatoes are subject to whilst being imported. The conditions that the amendment seeks to impose for the importation of table potatoes are as follows: 

 10. Admittedly, the petitioner being a citizen of Bangladesh carries on business of importer and distributor of food grains and crops including table potatoes through his proprietorship firm under the name and style "M/s. Panama Enterprise". It is the case of the petitioner that he filed an application before the respondent No.1 for issuance of import permit under Rules 3 and 5 of the Destructive Insects and Pests Rules, 1966 upon payment of requisite fees of Taka 310 through Government Treasury Chalan No. GaDa2/12 dated 29-10-2000 as evidenced by Annexures-B(1) and B(2). Rule 3 of the aforesaid Rules provides that no person shall import any plant and plant products which may be a source or medium of infection or infestation by diseases and plant pests destructive to agriculture or medium for the introduction of noxious weeds, except under a valid import permit obtained prior to such importation and except through the prescribed ports. Rule 5 lays down the procedure to be followed for making an application for permit in prescribed Form to the Director or Deputy Director (Quarantine). Rule 7 enumerates the grounds for which a permit to import plant or plant products may be revoked. In the instant case the petitioner filed an application before the respondent authority upon payment of requisite fees for issuance of import permit on 29-10-2000 and thereafter on many occasions he sent reminders to the respondents for issuance of import permit so that he could pursue his business but in spite of his repeated reminders the respondents remained silent without disposing of the said application for issuance of an import permit. It appears that the respondent No. 1 has failed to give a decision on the petitioner's application for import permit. It is asserted on behalf of the petitioner that under the Import Policy Order, 1997-2002 and SRO issued by the respondent No. 2 under the Import and Export Control Act 1950, table potatoes are freely importable. It appears that the petitioner filed an application in prescribed Form with a requisite fee of Taka 310 through Treasury Chalan No. GaDa2/12 dated 29-10-2000 as evidenced by Annexure-B series for issuance of import permit giving a tentative time-frame of the arrival of the first consignment on 15-11-2000 and the 2nd consignment on 30-11-2000 but in the Supplementary-Affidavit the petitioner stated that he being a businessman by profession is still in business though the tentative time-frame within which the petitioner originally intended to import the potatoes from India has elapsed, the petitioner is still intending to import potatoes from India in the current season and forthcoming season and, as such, the cause of action is still subsisting. He also stated in the Supplementary Affidavit that the government framed a new Import Policy Order namely, Import Policy Order 2002-2006 rendering the table potatoes to be a freely importable item. He is still ready and willing to import table potatoes from India and undertakes to comply with all the rules and regulations applicable for importation of table potatoes into Bangladesh. The Destructive Insects and Pests Act 1914 has been enacted to prevent introduction into Bangladesh of any insect, fungus or other pest which is or may be destructive to crops. Section 3 of the Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914 provides that the Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, prohibit or regulate, subject to such restrictions and conditions as it may impose, the import into Bangladesh or any part thereof, or any specified place therein, of any article or class of articles likely to cause infection to any crops or of insects generally or any class of insects. Sub-section (2) of section 3 provides that a notification under this section may specify any article or class of articles or any insect or class of insects either generally or in any particular manner, whether with reference to the country of origin; or the route by which imported. The Destructive Insects and Pests Rules 1966 has been framed under sub-section (1) of sections 3, 4(A) and 4(D) of the Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914. We have already noticed that under the aforesaid provision of law no person shall import any plant or plant products like table potatoes except under a valid import permit obtained prior to such importation issued by the Director or the Deputy Director (Quarantine) Plant Protection Wing. In the instant case, it appears that the petitioner filed an application with requisite fees for issuance of import permit for importation of table potatoes from India to Bangladesh. It also appears from the Import Policy Order 1997-2002 promulgated by the respondent No. 2 that table potatoes are freely importable subject to conditions as set out in table 'Kha' of the Import Policy which includes Phytosanitary Certificate obtained from the country of origin declaring that the crops from which consignment is derived was not grown in the vicinity of unhealthy potato crops and was inspected by a duly authorised official of phyto pathological service of the country of origin and found free from all injurious insects and no case of occurrence of the insects or disease was recorded within 5 kilometres of the place in which the potato crop was grown up as per Rule 14. In the instant case, the respondent No.1 is vested with power to issue import permit to the petitioner under the relevant provisions of law. It is true that if a particular plant or plant products is a source of medium of infection or infestation by diseases and plant pests destructive to agriculture or medium for the introduction of noxious weeds, the Appropriate Authority is very much empowered to refuse the grant of import permit. But in the instant case though the petitioner filed an application for issuance of import permit the respondent No. 1 sat over the matter without passing any order on the application of the petitioner. In other words, the respondent-authority was duty bound to issue import permit or to make a decision on the application of the petitioner but they have slept over the matter and thereby became guilty of laches which is not permissible in law. When an authority is vested with a power to issue a permit like the present case that authority should not sleep over the matter and should not suffer from inaction as it is duty bound to decide the matter in accordance with law. In the instant case the respondents failed to give a decision on the application of the petitioner and thereby suffered from inaction and that the inaction of the respondent No. 1 is violative of Destructive Insects and pests Act, 1914 and the Destructive Insects and Pests Rules, 1966 and, as such, the same shall be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no lawful effect.
